title: Luonnontieteellisen museon Elämän historia -sali sulkeutuu tammikuussa – uusi näyttely avautuu loppuvuodesta 2028
content:
The Natural History Museum’s History of Life is one of the museum’s most popular exhibitions. However, the exhibition, completed in 2008, has long been in need of an update, as it is outdated both in terms of content and exhibition technology.

– The new exhibition will present evolution and the development of biodiversity in a more spectacular and tangible way than before. This is the museum’s most significant renewal project in years, says Sanna Vuori, Head of the Public Engagement Unit at the Finnish Museum of Natural History.

The dinosaurs Giganotosaurus carolinii and Shunosaurus lii in the History of Life exhibition have become familiar to many museum visitors over the years. They will remain in the new exhibition but will be joined by never-before-seen reconstructions of prehistoric animals. Among other things, a reconstruction of the otter-like early whale Ambulocetus natans is currently being built in the museum’s conservation facilities.

title: Southnord Artfest 2026: Roots en Route
content:
Plants have always travelled – with the wind, with animals and birds, with humans. They have been carried across oceans, taken from their habitats and replanted to serve trade and empire.

Roots en Route is a multi-sensory installation by four artists who will create a multi-sensory installation in dialogue with the greenhouses – examining rootedness and displacement; asking what grows where it was planted and what survives the crossing. The African plants that fill the greenhouses carry their own histories of movement and adaptation.

Camille Norment in collaboration with Sofia Jernberg create a soundscape drawing on the insects and birds of the plants' homelands. Toubab Holmes' site-specific scent installation traces the hidden journeys of plants through the extractive system of perfumery. Charmaine Watkiss visits the botanical legacies and healing traditions of her Caribbean ancestry through large-scale drawings of Plant Warriors. Together, the three works read the botanical garden as an archive of movement, and the plants in it as things that were carried, taken and made to travel.

title: “Ilman pölyttäjiä maailma olisi ankea ja väritön” – Uusi näyttely avaa oven pölyttäjien kiehtovaan elämään
content:
Pollinators represent an astonishingly diverse group of animals, many of which possess remarkable abilities despite their small size. Bees can count, bumblebees solve problems, and on distant islands, even lizards can pollinate flowers.

The  exhibition, which combines science and art, offers a wealth of information, stunning visuals, and fun activities for visitors of all ages. Guests can play interactive games like "Identify the Pollinators" and "Pollinator Protection Bingo," design their own imaginary pollinator, and explore the museum's impressive collection of specimens. The exhibition is based on a newly illustrated non-fiction book.

– We want to show the world through the eyes of pollinators, says exhibition scriptwriter Mia Rönkä, Adjunct Professor in Environmental Ecology at the University of Turku. Rönkä has written the exhibition’s informational texts and poems.

Although the sensory perceptions, cognitive abilities, and communication methods of pollinators like bees differ from ours as humans, we can still strive to understand and appreciate them as individuals of other species – without anthropomorphizing them, Rönkä explains.

title: Ukrainan sota - yliopiston suositukset
content:
The University of Helsinki has condemned the military action by Russia and expressed its support for Ukraine and its university community. We have also expressed our support for Ukraine, together with other Finnish universities, through statements by and the . As a demonstration of support, we have illuminated buildings in the colours of the Ukrainian flag and raised the flag on our premises.

One of the principles of the University of Helsinki is to promote international collaboration in research and higher education, and to support these efforts even in difficult circumstances. Russia’s indefensible military aggression in Ukraine has required exceptional measures, which include those taken in the collaboration between universities.

The University of Helsinki is monitoring both national and EU-level sanctions, adapting our policies and processes accordingly. Together with other Finnish and international universities, the University of Helsinki strives to promote the end of military action in Ukraine, while supporting Ukrainian institutions and people.

title: Visiting the Music in Human and Social Development Research Group in Edinburgh
content:
Una Europa is a network of European universities dedicated to creating innovative research opportunities and learning experiences. Its Focus Areas represent interdisciplinary fields that bring together researchers from partner institutions across a wide range of disciplines.

Last spring, Una Europa Helsinki offered research mobility grants to foster collaboration between partner universities. Among the grant recipients, Doctoral Researcher Cesc Bayle from the BML research group had the opportunity to visit the Music in Human and Social Development (MHSD) research group at the University of Edinburgh, hosted by Prof. Katie Overy. The visit aimed to strengthen collaboration between the two research groups, particularly in the field of music education interventions focusing on improvisation.

title: HELDIG Summit 2026 Methodological encounters: Application deadline for talks and posters extended
content:
Dear reader,

We are gathering speakers and poster proposals for the next HELDIG Summit that aims to provide a snapshot of digital research in Social Sciences and Humanities today. To bring about discussion, we are planning three themes: digital history, digital social sciences and digital heritage. We invite you to contribute to this event with a 5-minute flash-talk or poster from recent or ongoing project(s). The Summit is a good opportunity to give visibility to your latest research and tools, get inspired by methodological innovations in similar fields, and make new connections.  

The HELDIG Summit brings together social sciences and humanities in a day that takes a snapshot at the state of the art in digital research. This year, we bring discussion around methodological and infrastructure encounters beyond disciplines. What challenges in data processing new methods enable us to overcome? How to maintain and adapt our research tools to fast-changing technological landscape? How to target the use of AI responsibly in the research cycle?  

The Summit will take place on December 4 (10:00-18:00), including a cocktail reception.
creator: wartvan@helsinki.fi

title: Two of our research infrastructures, SMEAR II and Pallas, have been awarded ACTRIS National Facility Labels!
content:
We’re proud to announce that two of our research infrastructures, SMEAR II and Pallas, have been awarded ACTRIS National Facility Labels!

The plaques were presented during the annual Week in Katowice, Poland, which brought together experts to discuss how to further develop, utilize and harmonize atmospheric observations of aerosols, clouds and trace gases.

These discussions are essential for strengthening atmospheric research and improving our understanding of the atmosphere.

Congratulations to everyone involved!

title: Elinympäristön laatu selittää Suomen lajiston vaihtelua enemmän kuin ilmasto
content:
Researchers at the University of Helsinki wanted to understand which is the dominant factor for species occurrence and abundance: the climate or habitat-related variables, such as their natural state and the share of land shaped by human activity. Solutions to mitigate biodiversity loss depend on the answer to this question.

Contrary to the researchers' expectations, habitat composition offers a better explanation than the climate for the occurrence and abundance of most animal groups. This conclusion highlights the importance of land-use planning in safeguarding biodiversity.

“The habitat proved to be of special importance to butterflies, birds, and small mammals. As for large mammals and moths, the relative importance of the habitat and climate were equal,” explains Emy Guilbault, the article’s lead author.

The study examined 503 terrestrial animal species, including changes in their occurrence, over a period of 20 years. The data covered the whole of Finland with all its climatic zones.  Analysing more than three million observations required the use of advanced statistical methods.

title: Albania’s future: from a mixed system to an EU member?
content:
In October 2026, several government buildings were set on fire in Tirana, Albania. For months, young Albanians had protested Jared Kushner’s planned multi-billion luxury resort on the island of Sazan and the nearby Vjosa-Narta coastal area. What began as an environmentalist and anti-corruption movement soon sprung into a wide unrest against the government and Albanian officials’ lack of transparency in public procurement and in general – The Flamingo Revolution, named after the birds living on Sazan, whose pictures the dissatisfied citizens have carried on their protest signs. 

Freedom of assembly is at the core of rule of law, as is transparency in public procurement and decision-making. Yet, there has been wide violence between police and the protesters, especially in the last two weeks. Prime minister Edi Rama, whose government aims for European Union membership by 2030, has claimed the protests are fuelled by disinformation and foreign interference. One of the protesters’ main aims is Rama’s resignation.
